# dstebz

> Computes the eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix T.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dstebz from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dstebz';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dstebz(
    range, order,
    N,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    d, strideD,
    e, strideE,
    M,
    nsplit,
    w, strideW,
    IBLOCK, strideIBLOCK,
    ISPLIT, strideISPLIT,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `range` | `("all"\|"value"\|"index")` | in |  |  | `'all'`: ("All") all eigenvalues will be found. `'value'`: ("Value") all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (VL, VU] will be found. `'index'`: ("Index") the IL-th through IU-th eigenvalues (of the entire matrix) will be found. |
| `order` | `("block"\|"entire")` | in |  | one of `'block'`, `'entire'` | storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | the order of the tridiagonal matrix T. |
| `vl` | `number` | in |  |  | if `range === 'value'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. |
| `vu` | `number` | in |  |  | if `range === 'value'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. |
| `il` | `integer` | in |  |  | if `range === 'index'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. 1 <= IL <= IU <= N, if N > 0. |
| `iu` | `integer` | in |  |  | if `range === 'index'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. 1 <= IL <= IU <= N, if N > 0. |
| `abstol` | `number` | in |  |  | the absolute tolerance for the eigenvalues. |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | the n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T. |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | the (n-1) off-diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T. |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `e` |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | the actual number of eigenvalues found. 0 <= M <= N. |
| `nsplit` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | the number of diagonal blocks in the matrix T. 1 <= NSPLIT <= N. |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | on exit, the first M elements of W will contain the eigenvalues. |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `w` |
| `IBLOCK` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | at each row/column j where E(j) is zero or small, the matrix T is considered to split into a block diagonal matrix (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideIBLOCK` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IBLOCK` |
| `ISPLIT` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | the splitting points, at which T breaks up into submatrices (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideISPLIT` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `ISPLIT` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 4 * N` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `4 * N` elements |
| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 3 * N` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `3 * N` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: ("All")   all eigenvalues will be found.
  -   `= 'V'`: ("Value") all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`, `VU`\] will be found.
  -   `= 'I'`: ("Index") the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues (of the entire matrix) will be found.
- `order`:

  -   `= 'B'`: ("By Block") the eigenvalues will be grouped by split-off block (see `IBLOCK`, `ISPLIT`) and ordered from smallest to largest within the block.
  -   `= 'E'`: ("Entire matrix") the eigenvalues for the entire matrix will be ordered from smallest to largest.
- `N`: The order of the tridiagonal matrix T. $N \ge 0$.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. Eigenvalues less than or equal to `VL`, or greater than `VU`, will not be returned. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. Eigenvalues less than or equal to `VL`, or greater than `VU`, will not be returned. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute tolerance for the eigenvalues. An eigenvalue (or cluster) is considered to be located if it has been determined to lie in an interval whose width is `ABSTOL` or less. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then ULP\*\|T\| will be used, where \|T\| means the 1-norm of T.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero.
- `d`: The n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `e`: The (n-1) off-diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `M`: The actual number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. (See also the description of `INFO=2`,3.)
- `nsplit`: The number of diagonal blocks in the matrix T. $1 \le \mathrm{NSPLIT} \le N$.
- `w`: On exit, the first M elements of W will contain the eigenvalues. (DSTEBZ may use the remaining N-M elements as workspace.)
- `IBLOCK`: At each row/column j where `E(j)` is zero or small, the matrix T is considered to split into a block diagonal matrix. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `IBLOCK(i)` specifies to which block (from 1 to the number of blocks) the eigenvalue `W(i)` belongs. (DSTEBZ may use the remaining N-M elements as workspace.)
- `ISPLIT`: The splitting points, at which T breaks up into submatrices. The first submatrix consists of rows/columns 1 to `ISPLIT(1)`, the second of rows/columns `ISPLIT(1)`+1 through `ISPLIT(2)`, etc., and the `NSPLIT`-th consists of rows/columns `ISPLIT(NSPLIT-1)`+1 through `ISPLIT(NSPLIT)=N`. (Only the first `NSPLIT` elements will actually be used, but since the user cannot know a priori what value `NSPLIT` will have, N words must be reserved for `ISPLIT`.)

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "all", "value", "index"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "block", "entire"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dstebz.ndarray(
    range, order,
    N,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    M,
    nsplit,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    IBLOCK, strideIBLOCK, offsetIBLOCK,
    ISPLIT, strideISPLIT, offsetISPLIT,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork
) → integer
```

Computes selected eigenvalues of a real symmetric tridiagonal matrix T.
by bisection.

**Returns** `integer`: info

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "all", "value", "index"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "block", "entire"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: some or all of the eigenvalues failed to converge or were not computed: =1 or 3: Bisection failed to converge for some eigenvalues; these eigenvalues are flagged by a negative block number.  The effect is that the eigenvalues may not be as accurate as the absolute and relative tolerances.  This is generally caused by unexpectedly inaccurate arithmetic. =2 or 3: `RANGE='I'` only: Not all of the eigenvalues `IL`:`IU` were found. Effect: $M < \mathrm{IU}+1-\mathrm{IL}$ Cause:  non-monotonic arithmetic, causing the Sturm sequence to be non-monotonic. Cure:   recalculate, using `RANGE='A'`, and pick out eigenvalues `IL`:`IU`.  In some cases, increasing the PARAMETER "FUDGE" may make things work.
-   `= 4`: `RANGE='I'`, and the Gershgorin interval initially used was too small.  No eigenvalues were computed. Probable cause: your machine has sloppy floating-point arithmetic. Cure: Increase the PARAMETER "FUDGE", recompile, and try again.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dstebz from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dstebz';

// Symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal `d` and off-diagonal `e`:
const N = 4;
const d = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0 ] );
const e = new Float64Array( [ -1.0, -1.0, -1.0 ] );
const M = new Int32Array( 1 );
const nsplit = new Int32Array( 1 );
const w = new Float64Array( N );
const IBLOCK = new Int32Array( N );
const ISPLIT = new Int32Array( N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 4 * N );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 3 * N );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dstebz( 'all', 'entire', N, 0.0, 0.0, 1, N, 0.0, d, 1, e, 1, M, nsplit, w, 1, IBLOCK, 1, ISPLIT, 1, WORK, IWORK );
console.log( info, M[ 0 ], w );

// Using the ndarray interface:
info = dstebz.ndarray( 'all', 'entire', N, 0.0, 0.0, 1, N, 0.0, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0, M, nsplit, w, 1, 0, IBLOCK, 1, 0, ISPLIT, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( info, M[ 0 ], w );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSTEBZ`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSTEBZ computes the eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix T. The user may ask for all eigenvalues, all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`, `VU`\], or the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues.

To avoid overflow, the matrix must be scaled so that its largest element is no greater than overflow\*\*(1/2) \* underflow\*\*(1/4) in absolute value, and for greatest accuracy, it should not be much smaller than that.

See W. Kahan "Accurate Eigenvalues of a Symmetric Tridiagonal Matrix", Report CS41, Computer Science Dept., Stanford University, July 21, 1966.

</section>
